title: Overlap deduplication and source-priority scorer for token attribution
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Implement a deduplication and source-priority scoring layer inside the usage ingestion pipeline to resolve overlapping events from multiple upstream producers (API gateway, streaming proxies, SDK retries, webhook replays). The goal is to ensure deterministic per-request token attribution with minimal divergence between near-real-time metering and end-of-day settlement reports. This ticket contains design, implementation, monitoring, and a backfill plan for correcting prior overlap-induced misattribution.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scorer runs for every ingestion record and produces a single canonical attribution key within the streaming window
Late-arriving events (up to 48 hours) are reconciled without double-charging or losing tokens
Unit and integration tests cover source-priority scenarios and identical idempotency tokens across producers
End-to-end regression on selected customers shows per-day token variance < 0.1% after reconciliation
Runbook updated and a dashboard created to observe duplicate rate, resolved conflicts, and downstream billing adjustments
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight 'overlap-scorer' stage in the Kafka ingestion consumer that computes (1) source trust score, (2) ingest timestamp confidence window, (3) idempotency signature hash, and (4) payload similarity fingerprint
Scoring rules: prefer API gateway > dedicated ingress proxies > SDK events > webhook replays, with numeric tie-breakers based on latency and signature freshness
Maintain a sliding in-memory LRU of recent signatures per tenant (TTL configurable, default 10m) to short-circuit duplicates and reduce downstream load
For ambiguous cases, persist both candidates to a 'conflict' topic and run a deterministic resolution job (daily) that emits the final canonical event and any credits/debits required
Expose a 'source_priority' column and 'resolved_by' tag in the token ledger for auditability
Backfill: best-effort merge of past 30 days using the new scorer, write out correction records to the billing-adjustments topic and surface in Console adjustments tab

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Scorer state could increase consumer memory on high-QPS tenants. Mitigation: use tenant-sharded caches with configurable max-entries and fallback to probabilistic Bloom filter to detect likely duplicates

Risk: Over-eager dedup might drop legitimate rapid replays (retries after network partition). Mitigation: keep per-request lifecycle metadata (attempt_count, source_host) and only dedup within configured window; add metrics for 'dedup_skipped_due_to_policy'
Risk: Backfill touches historic invoices. Mitigation: cap auto-corrections to non-billing-impacting flags for first rollout; manual review for >$100 adjustments and customer-notification workflow
testing_plan: Unit tests for hashing/fingerprint invariants across SDK/HTTP payload variants
Integration tests simulating multi-source delivery and late-arrivals using the ingestion test harness
Load test with replayed production trace at 2x QPS to validate memory and latency characteristics
Canary: enable scorer for 2% of traffic (selected smaller tenants) and compare daily ledger against control group for 72 hours
Post-canary: run backfill for last 7 days to validate corrections flow before 30-day backfill
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — behind feature flag: deploy scorer consumer and metric instrumentation (no rewrites)
Phase 1 — trial canary: enable dedup logic for 2% traffic; monitor resolved conflicts and downstream consumer errors
Phase 2 — widen to 25% after operational signoff; enable auto-resolve for corrections below $threshold
Phase 3 — full rollout to all tenants and start 7-day backfill; schedule 30-day backfill after monitoring window
Rollback criteria: if daily billing variance > 0.5% for canary group or conflict-to-resolution ratio > 10% for 48h
